title: Oxidation State Energetics (E°_M³⁺/M²⁺) & Disproportionation of Cu⁺
topics: 3d Series Oxidation States Range (Sc +3 to Mn +2...+7; Maximum OS in periodic table +8 in OsO₄, RuO₄)
3.1 Standard Electrode Potentials (E°_M²⁺/M and E°_M³⁺/M²⁺ Thermodynamic Coupling)
Redox Stability Analysis: Mn³⁺/Mn²⁺ (+1.57 V oxidant), Cr³⁺/Cr²⁺ (-0.41 V reducer), Fe³⁺/Fe²⁺ (+0.77 V)
3.2 Disproportionation of Cu⁺(aq): 2Cu⁺(aq) ──► Cu²⁺(aq) + Cu(s) (E°_cell = +0.36 V)
Hydration Enthalpy Driving Force of Cu²⁺ (Δ_hyd H = -2121 kJ/mol vs -581 kJ/mol)
quickSummary: Transition elements show variable oxidation states because (n-1)d and ns energies are close. Maximum in 3d is +7 (MnO₄⁻); maximum in periodic table is +8 (OsO₄, RuO₄). Mn³⁺ is a strong oxidant (+1.57 V); Cr²⁺ is a strong reducer (-0.41 V). Cu⁺ spontaneously disproportionates to Cu²⁺ and Cu due to huge hydration enthalpy of Cu²⁺ (-2121 kJ/mol).
summary: Master variable oxidation states, redox potential trends, and the hydration-driven disproportionation of Cu⁺.

summaryBox.title: Oxidation State Energetics
summaryBox.takeaway: Mn shows max OS (+7) in 3d series; Os and Ru show max OS (+8) in periodic table. Mn³⁺ (+1.57 V) is oxidizing; Cr²⁺ (-0.41 V) is reducing.

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
$3d$ SERIES OXIDATION STATES
                       
   $\text{Sc}$ (+3)  $\text{Ti}$ (+2,3,4)  $\text{V}$ (+2,3,4,5)  $\text{Cr}$ (+2,3,4,5,6)  $\mathbf{\text{Mn} \text{ (+2,3,4,5,6,+7)}}$
   $\text{Fe}$ (+2,3,4,6)  $\text{Co}$ (+2,3,4)  $\text{Ni}$ (+2,3,4)  $\text{Cu}$ (+1,+2)  $\text{Zn}$ (+2)

                   $E^\circ_{\text{M}^{3+}/\text{M}^{2+}}$ REDOX STABILITY ANALYSIS
                   
   $\mathbf{\text{Mn}^{3+} / \text{Mn}^{2+} = +1.57\text{ V}}$  ──► Highly Positive: $\text{Mn}^{3+} (3d^4)$ is a **powerful Oxidizing Agent**
                                               seeking to reach stable half-filled $\text{Mn}^{2+} (3d^5)$.
   $\mathbf{\text{Cr}^{3+} / \text{Cr}^{2+} = -0.41\text{ V}}$  ──► Negative: $\text{Cr}^{2+} (3d^4)$ is a **powerful Reducing Agent**
                                               spontaneously oxidizing to stable $\text{Cr}^{3+} (t_{2g}^3)$.
   $\mathbf{\text{Fe}^{3+} / \text{Fe}^{2+} = +0.77\text{ V}}$  ──► Moderate: $\text{Fe}^{3+} (3d^5)$ is moderately stable relative to $\text{Fe}^{2+} (3d^6)$.
conceptBreakdown.content:
Transition elements display variable oxidation states because the energy difference between $(n-1)d$ and $ns$ orbitals is extremely small, allowing both subshells to participate in bond formation.
- **Maximum OS in 3d series**: +7 in Manganese ($\text{MnO}_4^-$).
- **Maximum OS in Periodic Table**: +8 in Osmium ($\text{OsO}_4$) and Ruthenium ($\text{RuO}_4$).
- **Standard Electrode Potential**: Reflects thermodynamic balance $\Delta_{\text{total}} H^\circ = \Delta_{\text{sub}} H + \Delta_i H_1 + \Delta_i H_2 + \Delta_{\text{hyd}} H^\circ$.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 3.2 The Disproportionation of Cu⁺(aq)
conceptBreakdown.title: 3.2 The Disproportionation of Cu⁺(aq)
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
DISPROPORTIONATION OF Cu⁺(aq)

2Cu⁺(aq) ──► Cu²⁺(aq) + Cu(s)    (E°_cell = +0.36 V)

Thermodynamic Energetics:
• Hydration Enthalpy of Cu²⁺(aq): Δ_hyd H = -2121 kJ/mol
• Hydration Enthalpy of Cu⁺(aq):  Δ_hyd H = -581 kJ/mol
• 2nd Ionization Enthalpy of Cu:  Δ_i H_2 = +1958 kJ/mol

Massive hydration energy release (-2121 kJ/mol) far exceeds Δ_i H_2 (+1958 kJ/mol).
conceptBreakdown.content:
Although $\text{Cu}^+(aq)$ has a stable $3d^{10}$ configuration, it is thermodynamically unstable in aqueous solution and undergoes rapid disproportionation:
$$\mathbf{2\text{Cu}^+(aq) \longrightarrow \text{Cu}^{2+}(aq) + \text{Cu}(s) \quad (E^\circ_{\text{cell}} = +0.36\text{ V})}$$
- **Thermodynamic Reason**: The Hydration Enthalpy of $\text{Cu}^{2+}(aq)$ ($\Delta_{\text{hyd}} H = -2121\text{ kJ/mol}$) is much more negative than that of $\text{Cu}^+(aq)$ ($\Delta_{\text{hyd}} H = -581\text{ kJ/mol}$). This massive hydration energy release far outweighs the second ionization enthalpy required to convert $\text{Cu}^+ \rightarrow \text{Cu}^{2+}$ ($+1958\text{ kJ/mol}$).

quickRevision: Max 3d OS is +7 in MnO₄⁻; Max periodic OS is +8 in OsO₄, RuO₄.
Cu⁺ disproportionates in water: 2Cu⁺ ──► Cu²⁺ + Cu (E° = +0.36 V).
High hydration enthalpy of Cu²⁺ (-2121 kJ/mol) drives Cu⁺ disproportionation.
